## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A nine-*juan* (catalog meta) / ten-*juan* (DILA) compiled commentary on the Lotus Sūtra by [大義](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A7%E7%BE%A9) Dàyì of the mid-Qīng Yānjīng (Beijing) Buddhist establishment, hailed in his lifetime as "*the great consummation of the Lotus*" (*fǎhuá zhī dàchéng* 法華之大成). The work is the principal mid-Qīng synthetic Lotus Sūtra commentary, drawing together the Tiāntái, Cí'ēn, and late-Míng critical-evaluative traditions into a unified expository treatment.

**Abstract**

Dàyì's *Dàchéng* is the most ambitious mid-Qīng synthetic Lotus Sūtra commentary and the principal Qīng-period continuation of the late-Míng Tiāntái-Pure Land synthetic project of Hānshān [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85) Déqīng and Ǒuyì [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) Zhìxù. The work draws on (1) the foundational Tiāntái commentarial corpus ([智顗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%A1%97) Zhìyǐ's *Xuányì* ([KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006)) and *Wénjù* ([KR6d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0014)), [湛然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B9%9B%E7%84%B6) Zhànrán's three subcommentaries); (2) the Sòng *shānjiā* tradition through Sìmíng [知禮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9F%A5%E7%A6%AE) Zhīlǐ; (3) the Sòng *Yàojiě* tradition of [戒環](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%92%E7%92%B0) Jièhuán; (4) the Yuán-Míng *kēzhù* tradition; (5) the late-Míng critical-evaluative apparatus of Hānshān Déqīng, [通潤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%80%9A%E6%BD%A4) Tōngrùn, and Ǒuyì Zhìxù; and (6) Dàyì's own Pure Land and Avataṃsaka-derived doctrinal commitments.

The compilation history's specific dating allows the work to be securely placed in the productive period 1728–1736. The work was carried in the Manji-zoku canonical apparatus alongside its associated navigational and glossarial apparatus ([KR6d0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0084) and [KR6d0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0086)), demonstrating its institutional standing in the mid-Qīng Beijing Buddhist establishment.
